name: Lying about height / dating app height
lead: Lying about height, or "height padding", is the practice of stating a taller height than one's measured height on a dating profile or in conversation. In looksmaxxing and dating-advice communities it is discussed as a response to the belief that height strongly affects romantic outcomes, particularly for men (see Heightpill).

Research on self-reported height in general finds that people tend to report being taller than they measure, with the size of the gap varying by height, age, sex and region.[1] Studies on partner preference have reported that many women favour taller male partners, and that shorter men are rated less favourably on average.[2] Published research specifically measuring height inflation on dating apps was not located for this article, and no studies of outcomes for people who state a taller height were found.
infobox: Self-report bias documented generally; dating-app outcomes untested

paras: Dating apps typically ask users to enter a height, and some allow filtering by it. Community discussions describe entering a figure a few centimetres or an inch or more above one's true height, sometimes rounding up to a threshold such as six feet. Because the practice is private and unverifiable, no reliable figure for how common it is among dating-app users was found.

A general reference work on human height notes that self-reported height tends to exceed measured height, and that the discrepancy differs by height, age, gender and region.[1] This is a finding about surveys and records in general, not specifically about dating profiles.

Sociological writing on height discrimination ("heightism", a term coined in 1971) summarises studies in which women's stated preferences favoured taller partners, and in which shorter men were rated less favourably than average-height and tall men. The same source notes that the link between height and attractiveness reflects cultural norms and is not universal; a study of the Hadza foragers found height did not feature in mate choice.[2]
No studies found. Related research exists on height and partner preferences in general.[2]

card.summary: Stating a taller height on a dating profile than you measure; common talk, almost no direct research.
card.note: No studies on dating-app outcomes of stating a taller height were found.

quick.overview:
Lying about height means listing a taller height than one's real one on a dating app or profile. Communities that believe height strongly affects dating discuss it as a workaround.

General research shows people tend to over-report height in surveys, and studies report that many women prefer taller men. No study of how inflated heights affect dating-app results was found.
quick.mechanism: Users enter a larger number in the profile height field or round up to a threshold height. Nothing verifies the figure until people meet.
quick.risks: Documented consequences are not studied. Discussions describe discovery at in-person meetings as the main risk. Dating apps' terms of service generally address misleading profile information.
